Selected Projects

004 / Method

Working Process

01
Step 01
Observe

Start with what is already there. Study the material, constraints, context, and conditions before making a decision.

03
Step 03
Build

Make the solution with care. Give each medium its own discipline, detail, and precision.

02
Step 02
Frame

Turn the observation into a clear question. Set the goal, limits, and direction before the work begins.

04
Step 04
Refine

Test the result, find what needs to change, and repeat until the intent and outcome feel aligned.

005 / Books
Currently on the shelf

Good reads,
better ideas

A lot of what I think about starts with a book. Sometimes it changes the way I see a problem, sometimes it sends me down a completely unexpected rabbit hole. I read across philosophy, science, fiction, history, and plenty of things I probably had no practical reason to learn about.

For me, reading is less about collecting knowledge and more about staying curious. A good book tends to stick around, quietly influencing how I think, create, and see the world long after I’ve finished the last page.

Philosophy Sci-Fi Statistics Design Theory Vedanta History

What people say

A few kind words from people I’ve had the chance to work, learn, and create with.

REVIEW

A really good person at heart. Always helpful, the way he explains things n difficult topics in simple way n by giving so many examples is amazing. His knowledge is so vast, he is such a great cook. His spiritual knowledge about topics is also very good. But one bad thing is that he sleeps very late.

Important Person from my list
Thanks for pointing it out, I need to hear this!
REVIEW

I showed up to our first meeting with a notebook and good intentions. Saahil showed up with a plan, clear milestones and a backup for the backup. The project went smoothly, so I have to admit the preparation worked.

Aryan R.
REVIEW

Working with Saahil was easy and friendly from day one. He explains technical things in plain language, which is a rare skill and a big relief for people like me who nod along in meetings and hope for the best.

Lukas M.
REVIEW

He has a knack for linking ideas from very different fields, and it somehow all makes sense by the end. I came for one answer and left with three better questions, which I am choosing to count as a bonus.

Mihir S.
REVIEW

Saahil is calm, kind and very organised. When a deadline started getting dramatic, he gently steered us back to what actually needed doing. I credit him with at least three saved evenings.

Emma W.
REVIEW

I asked for a rough sketch and received something that had already thought about dimensions, proportions and how it would be made. His idea of rough and my idea of rough are clearly not the same thing.

Vikram B.
REVIEW

He brings structure to brainstorming without taking the fun out of it. Even a casual chat leaves you with a clearer idea and a short list of next steps, which is more than most of my meetings manage.

Mateo G.
REVIEW

He can explain a complicated idea with a simple example, then somehow make the example more interesting than the idea. Learning with him feels like a good conversation, not a lecture.

Rohan J.
REVIEW

Saahil is curious, patient and genuinely helpful. He asks thoughtful questions, listens properly and follows through, which sounds basic but is surprisingly rare. Highly recommended, snacks optional.

Sofia R.
REVIEW

A technical problem, the bigger picture and a little philosophy on the side: he handles all three without making any of it feel heavy. I left with a solution and a slightly better view of life.
